title: Layered Span Lens: interactive request drilldown with service-layer stacking
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: SREs and product engineers struggle to quickly understand multi-service request failures and performance regressions in Redwood Console. Existing trace views show spans sequentially but lack a compact, service-layered presentation, scrubby timeline controls, and per-request cost/rollout context.

Goal: Ship a design pattern (Layered Span Lens) that lets users quickly drill into a single request with an interactive, stacked service-layer timeline, correlation-id driven filters, and contextual cards for rollout markers and per-request cost. The lens should support fast comparison between traces, keyboard-first navigation, and easy linking to logs/PRs/alerts.

Scope: UI prototype, interaction spec, accessibility pass, handoff artifacts for frontend and product analytics. Not in scope: backend tracing ingestion changes beyond existing span fields, or cost attribution engine work (we'll rely on precomputed per-request cost tag).
acceptance_criteria: Interactive timeline supports layer stacking by service, with separate lanes for infra, app, and db spans
Mini-map scrubber and zoom allowing 10ms resolution up to full trace length
Span focus panel shows span metadata, correlated logs link, and per-request cost estimate when available
Correlation-id filter quick pills: clicking a correlation id filters session-related traces across the workspace
Comparison mode: side-by-side lens for two traces with synchronized scrubber
Keyboard shortcuts for next/previous span, expand/collapse service layer, and open focused span details
Design assets and Figma prototype handed off with component spec and example API payloads
prototype_notes: Initial prototype demonstrates stacked lanes (service grouping) and collapsed service summary rows
Hovering a span displays inline latency distribution sparkline and first/last seen annotation
Mini-map shows density heatmap of span activity; scrubber snaps to span boundaries when zoomed in
Rollout markers (canary, rollout-batch) appear on timeline with hovercard linking to release details
design_decisions: Use service-layer stacking instead of purely chronological list to reduce vertical scanning for multi-service requests
Collapse low-value spans (e.g., 0ms client-side instrumentation) into summarized nodes to reduce noise
Support both span-by-span and aggregated view: default to aggregated when trace has >200 spans
Expose correlation-id as primary filter token in UI and deep-link URL param for shareability
tradeoffs: Stacking improves signal but may obscure strict chronological order — we add a synchronized time ruler to preserve temporal context
Aggregating low-duration spans saves space but can hide important microbehaviors; we include expand-to-list affordance
Synchronized comparison requires more memory for client; initial implementation will limit to two traces
handoff_items: Figma components with tokens and responsive breakpoints
Interaction spec (keyboard table, edge cases for >200 spans, zoom math)
Example JSON trace payload with service, span_id, parent_id, start_ns, duration_ns, annotations, correlation_ids, cost_tag
Acceptance criteria test script for design QA
